title: Metering dispute resolution and reconciliation runbook
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Background: Customers occasionally report billing disagreements (token counts, inference durations, or incorrect discounts). We need a clear, repeatable reconciliation and dispute resolution runbook that combines automated daily reconciliation, human investigation playbooks, and audit-grade evidence packaging for customers and SOC auditors.

Problem statement: Without a documented, end-to-end process we risk slow dispute SLAs, inconsistent outcomes, and lack of traceable artifacts required for compliance reviews. This ticket captures design, automated checks, manual investigation steps, permissions, and the artifact bundle format for audits.

Scope: Daily automated reconciliation of metering pipelines (ingest events -> usage records -> billing units), proof bundle format for disputes and auditors, support agent playbook for first-response and escalation, postmortem checklist for reconciliation failures.

Out of scope: Rewriting the metering pipeline itself (separate infra ticket), cryptographic signing infrastructure (covered in ENG-19430).

Proposed solution: 1) Automated daily reconciliation job (reconcile-daily) comparing source-of-truth event stream (raw usage events in eventstore), aggregated billing records (billing_db.usage_agg), and customer-exportable CSVs. Job produces daily delta reports and anomaly flags. 2) Dispute intake flow in Support Console: capture customer-submitted evidence, create internal investigation ticket with reconciliation artifacts link. 3) Investigation runbook with verifiable steps and checks. 4) Evidence bundle format (.tar.gz) with standardized files for auditors: manifest.json, reconciliation_report.csv, raw_events_window.jsonl, billing_records_window.csv, config_snapshot.txt, and access_audit.log. 5) RBAC for export endpoints and audit bundle downloads with 90-day short-lived presigned URLs and mandatory approver for bundles older than 365 days.

Data sources & definitions: - raw_events: eventstore/usage-events partitioned by customer_id and date. Includes fields: event_id, timestamp_utc, model, tokens_input, tokens_output, duration_ms, request_id, gateway_node. - billing_records: billing_db.usage_agg with fields: agg_id, window_start, window_end, customer_id, billed_tokens, billed_duration_ms, rate_plan_id, invoice_id. - customer_exports: CSVs produced by customer_export_service.

Reconciliation logic (high level): 1) Join raw_events to billing_records by request_id where present. 2) For unmatched events, aggregate tokens by window and compare to billing_records.billed_tokens. 3) Apply normalization rules: timezone canonicalization (UTC), clock skew tolerance (±5s), rounding policy for tokenization (round-half-up to nearest token unit), and discount application order. 4) Flag delta where absolute difference > 0.5% of billed_tokens AND > 100 tokens, or where billing duration differs by > 500ms per-request on aggregate. 5) Classify anomalies: MissingEvents, DoubleCount, PricingMismatch, AggregationWindowMismatch, ExportMismatch.

Investigation runbook (agent steps): - Step 0: Acknowledge within 24 hours (support SLA). - Step 1: Pull daily reconciliation report for customer_id and window. - Step 2: If anomaly type MissingEvents: query raw_events for request_id and gateway_node; check ingestion pipeline lag (observability trace). - Step 3: If DoubleCount: inspect intermediate aggregator logs (aggregator_X logs) for duplicate ingestion markers (dedupe_id). - Step 4: If PricingMismatch: verify effective rate_plan at window_start/time by consulting billing_config_history. - Step 5: If AggregationWindowMismatch: confirm scheduled cron jobs and broker offset metrics. - Step 6: Collate supporting artifacts and produce evidence bundle following Evidence Format below. - Step 7: Communicate resolution to customer with root cause and remediation, and optionally issue credit.

Evidence bundle format (required files): - manifest.json: keys: customer_id, windows, generated_at, generator_service, correlation_id. - reconciliation_report.csv: row schema [window_start, window_end, billed_tokens, actual_tokens, delta_tokens, anomaly_type, investigator]. - raw_events_window.jsonl: raw usage events for the investigated window (newline-delimited JSON). - billing_records_window.csv: matching rows from billing_db. - config_snapshot.txt: snapshot of pricing rules and rate plan effective at window_time. - access_audit.log: who downloaded this bundle and presigned URL expiry.

Access controls & retention: - Evidence bundles stored in secure audit bucket (GCS/Azure): path pattern gs://redwood-audit/bundles/{customer_id}/{YYYY}/{MM}/{DD}/{bundle_id}. - Default retention policy: 5 years for audit bundles for enterprise customers; 2 years for standard customers. - Download requires "billing_audit_viewer" role; downloads generate an entry in access_audit.log and send Slack alert to oncall-billing for bundles older than 180 days. - Presigned URLs are short-lived by default (90s); a support approver can extend to 24 hours for active investigations.

Monitoring & alerting: - Daily reconciliation job reports to billing-integrity dashboard with success/fail counts, total deltas, and anomaly rate. Alert thresholds: >0.2% customers flagged in a day triggers P1 alert. - Pager duty flow for job failures: engineering-sre -> billing-team -> PM.

Acceptance criteria: - Automated daily reconciliation job runs on schedule and publishes delta reports. - Support Console links directly to generated reconciliation report for a selected customer window. - Evidence bundle generator produces correct manifest.json and required artifacts for at least three sample cases (MissingEvents, PricingMismatch, DoubleCount). - RBAC enforced for bundle downloads; downloads logged and monitored. - Runbook documented in Confluence and approved by Legal/Compliance.

Rollout plan: 1) Canary: run reconcile-daily in shadow mode for 2 weeks on 5% customers. 2) Validate canary outputs with manual spot checks against invoice samples. 3) Turn on alerting and support console links for beta customers (10 accounts). 4) Full rollout after two successful cycles and signoff from Compliance.

Trade-offs and alternatives considered: - Stronger cryptographic proofs (Merkle trees) considered but deferred to a separate project to keep this scope actionable. - Shorter retention reduces storage cost but increases risk for audits; settled on 5y/2y split per customer tier.

Open questions: - Does Finance require CSVs in a specific schema for disputes? (Action: PM to confirm with Finance by 2026-03-05). - Should we encrypt evidence bundles with customer-specific KMS keys? (Security preferred; needs integration effort.)
acceptance_criteria: 1) reconcile-daily job scheduled and green on production for 7 consecutive days; 2) support console shows reconciliation_report link and evidence bundle download for a test customer; 3) evidence bundle schema validated with legal and compliance; 4) RBAC tests demonstrating only billing_audit_viewer can download; 5) alerting triggers when anomaly rate >0.2%.
